events.title: U.S. Constitution Signed in Philadelphia
events.description: After a long summer of debate, delegates to the Constitutional Convention met for the last time and signed the document that created the framework of the United States government.
events.significance: The Constitution is now the oldest written national constitution still in use. The U.S. marks the anniversary each year as Constitution Day and Citizenship Day.

events.title: Battle of Antietam
events.description: Union and Confederate armies fought near Sharpsburg, Maryland, in a battle that became the bloodiest single day in American military history.
events.significance: The Union's narrow strategic victory stopped Robert E. Lee's first invasion of the North. It gave President Lincoln the opening to issue the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation.

events.title: First Fatality in a Powered Airplane Crash
events.description: Lt. Thomas Selfridge was a passenger in a Wright Flyer piloted by Orville Wright during Army trials at Fort Myer, Virginia. A propeller failure caused the crash, and Selfridge died of his injuries.
events.significance: Selfridge became the first person to die in a powered airplane crash. The accident led to stricter attention to aircraft safety and design.

events.title: Camp David Accords Signed
events.description: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin signed two agreements at the White House. U.S. President Jimmy Carter had brokered them after nearly two weeks of talks at Camp David.
events.significance: The accords led to the 1979 Egypt-Israel peace treaty, the first peace agreement between Israel and an Arab state, and reshaped Middle East diplomacy.
